Incorporating the May 2017 Beige Book alongside the FOMC’s June statement and April SLOOS:

- Beige Book confirms modest-to-moderate growth across most districts, with employment reported up and labor markets tight, especially for skilled workers where wage pressures are more evident. This reinforces the FOMC’s view of continued labor-market strengthening.
- Sectorally, housing activity generally outpaced commercial real estate, which was more mixed—consistent with SLOOS reports of tighter conditions and caution in CRE. Auto-related credit also showed tighter standards, aligning with softer auto activity.
- Energy sectors improved, supporting manufacturing and related activity in several districts; tourism activity (e.g., New York) also contributed to steady growth.
- Lending volumes broadly mirrored the pace of the economy, with standards little changed on net—some offset from easing in consumer credit cards and willingness to lend on installment loans.
- Inflation and wage gains remained modest overall despite tight labor markets, echoing the FOMC’s below-2% inflation reading and “monitoring closely” stance.

Net effect: The Beige Book slightly strengthens the otherwise mildly positive macro narrative (labor-market breadth, energy rebound, steady lending volumes), but persistent low inflation and mixed CRE/auto conditions keep the tone cautious. I nudge the assessment modestly higher from 0.30 to 0.35.
